name: GMO GPU Cloud
ownership: Public (TSE: 4784), part of GMO Internet Group (TSE: 9449)
snippet: Japanese GPU cloud run by Tokyo-listed GMO Internet with METI subsidy backing. It added NVIDIA B300 servers in December 2025 and plans a second site at a 15 MW renewable data center in Hokkaido.
origin: Masatoshi Kumagai founded GMO Internet Group in Tokyo in 1991, and the group built its business on domains, hosting and internet access. It first rented GPUs in March 2019 through GPU Cloud byGMO, a small NVIDIA V100 service. In April 2024 Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry certified the group's plan to supply H200 cloud capacity under its economic security cloud program, with a subsidy of up to ¥1.925B toward a build of about ¥10B. GMO GPU Cloud launched on November 22, 2024 with 768 H200 GPUs and placed 37th on the TOP500 list that month.
today: GMO Internet, Inc., the Tokyo-listed group company that took over the infrastructure business in January 2025, runs the service. In August 2025 it dropped a planned purchase of 256 more H200 GPUs and ordered 200 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in 25 servers instead. B300 bare metal servers went on sale on December 16, 2025, and a managed Slurm plan on B300 followed in March 2026. In February 2026 GMO invested ¥3.2B in the autonomous driving startup Turing and signed a four-year contract to supply it about 0.37 EFLOPS of H200 and B300 capacity. Sakana AI trained the alpha version of its Japanese Namazu models on the service, and AIST bought about ¥68.5M of GPU cloud capacity and support for February and March 2026. In October 2026 GMO announced a second site at a 15 MW data center in Ishikari, Hokkaido, which runs on 100% renewable power and links to Tokyo over NTT East's IOWN network.
platform: The service runs NVIDIA HGX H200 and HGX B300 servers on NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet with BlueField-3 DPUs and DDN shared storage, and GMO was the first Japanese cloud to adopt Spectrum-X. Customers choose a managed HPC cluster with Slurm preinstalled or a dedicated bare metal server, and GMO quotes GPU prices individually. During 2025 and 2026 it added MIG partitioning, a private container registry, Grafana dashboards, Enroot and Pyxis container support, and EDR security monitoring. GMO's own tests show the B300 finishing a Llama 2 70B LoRA fine-tuning run about twice as fast as the H200.
outlook: GMO, TOKYU LAND and BroadBand Tower aim to start GPU service in Ishikari within 2026, which moves capacity beyond the Tokyo area where new grid connections are hard to secure. GMO has not disclosed how many GPUs it will place at the new site. Long-term deals such as the four-year Turing contract and the AIST work give the service committed demand while it adds Blackwell capacity.

editor_notes: The seed said H200 and B200. GMO never offered B200, and in August 2025 it switched a planned H200 expansion (256 GPUs, about ¥1.5B, announced May 2025) to 200 B300 GPUs. The seed launch date of November 2023 is wrong, since the service launched on November 22, 2024. GMO Internet, Inc. (TSE: 4784, formerly GMO AD Partners) runs the service and is a listed member of GMO Internet Group (TSE: 9449). I did not verify the group's exact stake. The subsidy figure is the April 2024 METI award of up to ¥1.925B, and I did not find a later METI award for the B300 purchase. Founded is the service launch year, and the parent group dates to 1991. I chose devcloud because the operator mainly sells hosting, domains and access, with GPU cloud as one line. GMO does not publish a current total GPU count or the GPU count planned for Ishikari.

name: FPT AI Factory
ownership: Public (HOSE: FPT), run by FPT Smart Cloud
snippet: GPU cloud from Vietnam's FPT Corporation with NVIDIA clusters in Vietnam and Japan. It lists more than 3,000 NVIDIA GPUs and sells HGX B300 capacity from $6.99 per GPU-hour in 2026.
origin: FPT Corporation began in Hanoi in 1988 and grew into a technology group with IT services, telecom and education arms and about 80,000 staff. In April 2024 it agreed a $200M partnership with NVIDIA to build AI factories, and its cloud unit FPT Smart Cloud took on the project. FPT launched FPT AI Factory in Japan in November 2024 on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, with a partner group that included SCSK, HPE, ASUS, VAST Data and DDN.
today: FPT AI Factory runs H100 and H200 clusters in Vietnam and Japan and lists more than 3,000 NVIDIA GPUs on its website. On the June 2025 TOP500 list its H200 system in Japan placed 36th at 49.85 PFLOPS and its H100 system in Vietnam placed 38th at 46.65 PFLOPS. CRN Asia reported in March 2026 that FPT was adding NVIDIA HGX B300 clusters, and the B300 now appears on its price list at $6.99 per GPU-hour. FPT added RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell virtual machines by August 2026 and lists Malaysia as a coming location. CRN Asia puts the service at 43 AI cloud services used by more than 18,000 engineers, scientists and business users. In October 2026 FPT signed a memorandum with NAVER Cloud to cooperate on AI factory and GPU as a service business in Korea, Japan and Vietnam.
platform: Customers can rent GPU containers, GPU virtual machines, dedicated bare metal servers under the Metal Cloud name, and Kubernetes-managed GPU clusters with InfiniBand. FPT also sells serverless and dedicated inference for more than 20 models and an AI Studio for building and fine-tuning models. The Japan cluster uses HPE servers with H200 GPUs and the Vietnam cluster uses ASUS servers with H100 GPUs, both on NDR400 InfiniBand. FPT lists DDN and VAST Data among its storage partners.
outlook: FPT says it is deploying B300 clusters across Japan and Vietnam and will open in Malaysia, but it does not publish GPU counts for each site. The NAVER Cloud memorandum covers joint AI factory and GPU as a service work, and neither company has disclosed financial terms. Digital in Asia reports that FPT belongs to a consortium with G42, VinaCapital and Viet Thai behind a proposed $2.1B hyperscale AI data center in Ho Chi Minh City.

editor_notes: I chose neocloud over sovereign because FPT is a listed company (HOSE: FPT) led by founder and chairman Truong Gia Binh, with no controlling state shareholder in the sources I checked, and it sells the service commercially. FPT does market the service as sovereign AI. The seed called FPT private, but it is publicly listed and privately controlled. I could not verify the seed claim that FPT uses Nebius Soperator, since its product pages and docs mention Kubernetes but not Slurm or Soperator, so the profile omits it. I found no evidence of B200 or GB200 deployments, and B300 appears on the price list. Founded is the AI Factory launch year, and FPT Corporation dates to 1988. The $200M figure comes from Wikipedia and secondary press, not an FPT release I could fetch. The G42 consortium claim rests on one secondary source. The Tokyo, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City addresses on the site are offices, and FPT does not publish its data center locations.

name: VESSL AI
snippet: Korean MLOps company turned GPU cloud that says it runs more than 8,000 GPUs across 20+ clouds. In September 2026 it sought about $150M in Series C funding to build its own data center.
origin: An Jaeman founded VESSL AI in Seoul in 2020 with engineers from Sendbird and Google to sell MLOps software for training, serving and scheduling models. Its early pitch was cutting GPU bills by up to 80% by spreading jobs across on-premises clusters, spot instances and several clouds. The company set up a US entity in 2021, and An moved to the US in September 2024 to lead US operations. In October 2024 it raised a $12M Series A, bringing total funding to $16.8M, and by 2026 it sold GPU capacity directly under the VESSL Cloud name.
today: VESSL Cloud rents A100, L40S and H100 GPUs on demand and reserves H200, B200, B300, GB200 NVL72 and GB300 capacity for larger clusters. At a Samsung SDS event in September 2026, An said the company runs more than 8,000 GPUs and grew revenue more than 50 times over the prior year. It began supplying a 128-GPU B200 cluster to SK Biopharm in August 2026, and in October 2026 it took over global inference for Upstage's Solar Pro 4 model across Korea, Europe and the US. VESSL AI Korea joined the KT consortium, one of three that Korea's science ministry selected in August 2026 for its AI for All program, and the government is giving the three consortia 512 B200 GPUs this year. VESSL will also run the GPU platform for Neo AI Cloud's ₩600B Pohang AI data center, whose first 40 MW phase is due in November 2027. KED Global reported in September 2026 that VESSL is raising about $150M in Series C funding at a pre-money valuation near $370M, and that Korea's National Growth Fund is considering joining.
platform: VESSL Cloud sells container workspaces and batch jobs with per-second billing, VM clusters with 400 Gbps NDR InfiniBand and shared NFS storage up to 200 TiB, and provisioned inference throughput behind APIs compatible with the OpenAI and Anthropic formats. Its regions include us-west-2, eu-north1 and kr-west. VESSL says it aggregates capacity from more than 20 hyperscalers and neoclouds instead of owning one large fleet. In a joint project Samsung SDS ran the data center layer while VESSL handled scheduling and fault recovery, and VESSL says cluster utilization rose from 35% to 90%.
outlook: KED Global reports that VESSL plans to use the Series C money to build its own data center and grow to 10,000 GPUs. The Pohang site has a second phase planned at 260 MW, and VESSL is responsible for finding customers for it in Korea and abroad. KED Global reported only that the National Growth Fund is considering the deal, so the size and terms of the round are not settled. VESSL lists managed Kubernetes and Slurm as coming soon.

editor_notes: I chose platform because VESSL started as MLOps software and sells capacity it aggregates from more than 20 clouds through its own software. It now calls itself a neocloud and may fit that category once its own data center opens. I listed the HQ as Seoul because KED Global calls it a homegrown Korean startup in 2026 and its Korean government work runs through VESSL AI Korea. The parent is VESSL AI, Inc., a US entity that KED Global described in 2024 as the headquarters, with a San Mateo office, so I could not confirm the seed's Seoul and San Francisco pairing. I did not find a Series B announcement, though the $370M valuation suggests funding after the 2024 Series A. The 8,000 GPU and 50x revenue figures come from the CEO's remarks on VESSL's own blog. The 512 B200 GPUs go to all three AI for All consortia combined, not to VESSL alone. Neo AI Cloud owns the Pohang project, and VESSL is its GPU platform partner.
